text:
Tyler Toffoli has played for seven NHL teams and scored more than 300 goals, and on a Sharks team full of young forwards he's the veteran who still finishes. His tying goal against the Islanders on Sunday went in off an opponent's face (Yahoo Sports' words, not ours), and the Sharks won in a shootout to end a five-game skid. That's Toffoli's season in one shift: not pretty, usually useful.

He has 11 points in 20 games in about 13 minutes a night, four of them on the power play, and his production per minute (2.47 points per 60) is ahead of the league's typical forward. Nothing looks lucky. His goals are about where his chances say they should be, and his range for the season centres on 46 points, close to last year's 49. Our wins-added numbers put him 53rd among more than 500 skaters, a reminder that timely goals count. The one concern is speed: his top speed is in the bottom fifth of the league, and at 34 that doesn't come back.
